content: The global incidence and prevalence of medulloblastoma are approximately less than 1 per 100,000 individuals. Medulloblastoma is a rare disease that predominantly affects children. The likelihood of developing medulloblastoma decreases with increasing age, with the median age of diagnosis being 5 years. Males are more frequently affected by medulloblastoma compared to females, with a male-to-female ratio of approximately 2:1. Medulloblastomas occur at a rate of just under 2 cases per million individuals annually. Children are 10 times more likely to develop medulloblastoma compared to adults. Among pediatric brain tumors, medulloblastoma is the second most common after pilocytic astrocytoma and is the most common malignant brain tumor in children, accounting for 14.5% of newly diagnosed cases. In adults, medulloblastoma is exceedingly rare, representing fewer than 2% of all central nervous system (CNS) malignancies. In children, the incidence of medulloblastoma is higher in males (62%) compared to females (38%), a gender disparity that is not observed in adult cases. Medulloblastoma and other primitive neuroectodermal tumors (PNETs) are more prevalent in younger children compared to older children. Specifically, 40% of medulloblastoma cases are diagnosed in children under the age of 5, 31% in children aged 5 to 9, 18.3% in those aged 10 to 14, and 12.7% in adolescents aged 15 to 19.
